prompt: You double each register's data width but keep the same number of registers and ports. What changes in the teaching register file?

options.text: Read muxes become wider, while the register-number selection width stays the same
options.explanation: Correct. The same addresses choose larger values.

options.text: Twice as many register-number bits are required
options.explanation: Address width depends on the number of registers, not bits per register.

options.text: The write decoder needs one output for every data bit
options.explanation: Each decoder output enables a whole register.
Wider data does not remove the need to choose and access registers.

workedExample: Separate the address from the value. A register number still names one of the same set of registers. Each selected register now carries more data bits, so its storage and data paths widen while the decoder still chooses one register.
